t: The first Chinese dynasty known from its own writing, ruling the middle Yellow River plain from c. 1600 to 1046 BCE.
Its kings divined with inscribed oracle bones, the oldest substantial body of Chinese writing.
Its bronze ritual vessels, chariots and royal tombs at Anyang make it one of the great Bronze Age civilisations.
dyk: Before scholars recognised the writing on them around 1899, Shang oracle bones were ground up and sold by apothecaries as 'dragon bones' for medicine.
ev: Tang of Shang overthrows Jie of the Xia, according to tradition
The walled city at Zhengzhou flourishes in the Erligang period
Pan Geng moves the capital to Yin near Anyang
Wu Ding begins his long reign; the earliest oracle-bone inscriptions
Chariots appear at Anyang; Fu Hao is buried in her tomb
King Wu of Zhou defeats Di Xin at the Battle of Muye

f.capital: Zhengzhou and other early capitals; later Yin (Anyang)
